airport: Large paved runways and expansive terminal complexes with clearly marked taxiways and aprons distinguish it from the compact platform layout of a railway station, the linear elongated structure of a viaduct, and the natural meandering flow of a river.
beach: A narrow elongated strip of light-colored sand situated between the ocean and inland vegetation distinguishes it from the enclosed still water of a pond, the flowing linear channel of a river, and the large paved surfaces of an airport.
bridge: A linear structure spanning across a river or valley with visible pillars and deck connecting two land masses distinguishes it from the long elevated highway structure of a viaduct, and lacks the open paved areas of an airport or the natural water surface of a river.
commercial: Densely packed high-rise buildings with regular grid-like street patterns and rooftop structures distinguish it from the uniform rows of parked vehicles in a parking lot, the lower and more irregular residential rooftops, and the large single-story industrial warehouse rooftops.
desert: A vast homogeneous expanse of bare sandy or rocky terrain with sparse texture and no vegetation distinguishes it from the large flat paved surfaces of an airport, the linear water channel of a river, the dense building clusters of residential areas, and the green canopy texture of a forest.
farmland: Regularly arranged rectangular crop plots with alternating texture patterns and field boundaries distinguish it from the uniform short green grass texture of a meadow, the large paved runway surfaces of an airport, and the dense tree canopy of a forest.
footballfield: A rectangular green grass field with clearly visible white lane markings and surrounded by seating stands distinguishes it from the unmarked uniform green grass of a meadow, the large paved surfaces of an airport, and the irregular tree canopy patterns of a forest.
forest: Dense contiguous dark green tree canopy with rough textured crown patterns distinguishes it from the elevated terrain and ridgelines of a mountain, the regular crop row patterns of farmland, and the uniform short grass texture of a meadow.
industrial: Large single-story warehouse buildings with wide flat rooftops arranged in orderly rows alongside roads and loading areas distinguish it from the dense high-rise structures of commercial areas, the uniform parked vehicle patterns of a parking lot, and the organized residential housing blocks.
meadow: A broad open area of uniform short green grass with smooth texture and no distinct markings distinguishes it from the crop row patterns of farmland, the white lane markings on a football field, and the dense dark tree canopy of a forest.
mountain: Rugged terrain with irregular ridgelines, varying elevation shadows, and natural vegetation patches distinguishes it from the dense uniform canopy of a forest, the flat open expanse of a desert, and the regular geometric patterns of farmland.
park: Irregularly shaped green spaces with scattered trees, winding paths, and small water bodies distinguish it from the dense building clusters of residential areas, the large flat paved surfaces of an airport, and the uniform crop patterns of farmland.
parking: A flat paved area filled with uniformly arranged rows of small rectangular vehicles separated by lane markings distinguishes it from the dense high-rise rooftops of commercial areas, the organized building blocks of residential areas, and the large warehouse rooftops of industrial areas.
pond: A small enclosed irregularly shaped body of still water surrounded by land vegetation distinguishes it from the light-colored sandy strip of a beach, the linear flowing channel of a river, and the green grass texture of a meadow.
port: Linear dock structures extending into water with adjacent cargo storage areas and cranes distinguish it from the large paved runway surfaces of an airport, the linear spanning structure of a bridge, and the dense building clusters of commercial areas.
railwaystation: Multiple parallel railway tracks converging at platforms with an elongated station building distinguishes it from the expansive runway layout of an airport, the linear spanning structure of a viaduct, and the natural meandering flow of a river.
residential: Densely packed low-rise buildings with irregular rooftop shapes and narrow streets forming a complex network distinguish it from the dense high-rise structures of commercial areas, the large warehouse rooftops of industrial areas, and the uniform vehicle rows of a parking lot.
river: A long sinuous water channel with natural meandering curves and consistent flow direction distinguishes it from the narrow sandy strip of a beach, the small enclosed water body of a pond, and the linear spanning structure of a bridge.
viaduct: A long elevated linear structure with regularly spaced pillars casting shadows on the ground distinguishes it from the spanning structure of a bridge over water, the flat paved surfaces of an airport, and the dense building clusters of residential areas.
